The dedicated tools render in the per-tool permission UI and keep raw stdout out of the conversation; that is why they are worth reaching for whenever one fits.

**Output:**
The stdout and stderr will be combined and returned as a string. The output may be truncated if it is too long. If the command exits non-zero, the output ends with a `Command failed with exit code: N` line; a command killed by its timeout or interrupted by the user ends with its own message instead.

Background execution is disabled for this agent. Do not set `run_in_background=true`.

- Each shell tool call will be executed in a fresh shell environment. The shell variables, current working directory changes, and the shell history is not preserved between calls. Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension

args.command:
cat > /workspace/observed/undo-redo-reset-log-repair.md <<'SPEC_EOF'
# Observed behavior: `stg undo`, `redo`, `reset`, `log`, `repair` (StGit 2.5.5)

Reference binary: `/workspace/executable` (`Stacked Git 2.5.5`, git 2.34.1).
All experiments in throwaway repos (`git init`, `git commit --allow-empty -m initial`, `stg init`).
Conventions below: `$S` = the binary. Exit codes noted as `EXIT:n`. Unless noted,
stdout/stderr were separated with `1>/tmp/o.txt 2>/tmp/e.txt`.

## 0. Stack log structure (relevant to all 5 commands)

- Ref `refs/stacks/<branch>` points to a "full" log commit. Each user-visible log
  entry is a "simplified" commit with 1 parent (the previous simplified commit) and
  the entry message. The full commit has THREE parents:
  `[simplified-entry-commit, branch-head-commit, previous-full-commit]`, and its
  tree is the stack metadata tree (same tree as the simplified commit).
- `stg log` prints the **simplified** commit ids. `stg reset <id>` accepts both the
  simplified id (as printed by `stg log`) and the full 40-char id of the full commit.
- `stack.json` `"prev"` points to the previous FULL log commit (`null` after
  `stg init` / `stg log --clear`); `"head"` is the branch head commit.
- Log entry messages observed (all single-line): `initialize`, `new: <name>`,
  `pop`, `push`, `goto`, `delete`, `hide`, `unhide`, `rename <old> <new>`,
  `refresh <name>`, `refresh refresh-temp (create temporary patch)`,
  `refresh  (CONFLICT)`  (note TWO spaces before `(`; emitted when a refresh ends
  with merge conflicts), `undo <n>`, `redo <n>`, `reset`, `repair`,
  `external modifications`, `clear log`.
- IMPORTANT: `stg refresh` creates TWO log entries
  (`refresh refresh-temp (create temporary patch)` then `refresh <name>`), and
  `stg undo` steps back ONE LOG ENTRY, not one user command. So a single `stg undo`
  right after `stg refresh` lands in the intermediate state where a patch named
  `refresh-temp` is applied on top:

      $ $S new -m one p1 >/dev/null; $S refresh >/dev/null
      $ $S undo
      > refresh-temp
      $ $S series -a
      + p1
      > refresh-temp
      $ $S undo        # second undo reaches pre-refresh state
      > p1

- A failed/conflicted transaction still writes a log entry (e.g. `refresh  (CONFLICT)`).

## 1. `stg undo`

Help: "Reset the patch stack to the state before the last operation."
Options: `-n, --number <n>`, `--hard`, `--color <when>`. No `-b`, no positional args.

### Output
On success stdout is exactly ONE line: the topmost applied patch of the resulting
state, `> <name>\n`; if the resulting state has NO applied patches, stdout is EMPTY.
It never prints `+`/`-` lines for individual patches (unlike push/pop transactions).

    $ $S new -m three p3        # (stack: p1 p2 applied)
    > p3 (new)
    $ $S undo ; echo EXIT:$?
    > p2
    EXIT:0
    $ $S undo                   # now only p1 applied
    > p1
    $ $S undo                   # undid `new: p1`; empty stack -> NO output
    EXIT:0
    $ $S undo                   # nothing more to undo
    error: not enough undo information available
    EXIT:2                       # (stderr; stdout empty)

More scenarios (all print just the topmost line):
- undo after `stg pop` (p3 popped) -> `> p3`
- undo after `stg push` -> `> p2`
- undo after `stg delete p2` (was applied) -> `> p2`
- undo after `stg delete p3` (was unapplied; topmost unchanged) -> `> p2`  (still prints topmost)
- undo after `stg pop -a` -> `> p3`
- `$S undo -n 2` from (p1 p2 p3 applied) -> `> p1`, EXIT:0

Cannot undo the `initialize` entry itself: with only `initialize` in the log,
`stg undo` fails with `not enough undo information available`.

### Side effects
- Adds log entry `undo 1` (or `undo <n>`), updates `refs/stacks/<branch>`, the
  branch ref (HEAD) and the worktree to the recorded state.
- Undo preserves dirty worktree/index when the tree needn't change; if checkout
  would clobber local changes it fails and rolls back:

      $ $S undo        # file.txt locally modified, undo would restore it
      @ p1 (rolled back)                                  # stdout
      error: `git read-tree -m -u`: error: Entry 'file.txt' not uptodate. Cannot merge.;
      command aborted (all changes rolled back)           # stderr
      EXIT:2
      # variant with staged change: "error: Entry 'file.txt' would be overwritten by merge. Cannot merge.;"

- `--hard` discards index+worktree changes and succeeds:

      $ $S undo --hard
      > p2
      EXIT:0        # local modifications gone

### Error cases
- `$S undo -n 99` (more than available): stderr `error: not enough undo information available`, EXIT:2. Atomic — nothing is undone.
- `$S undo -n 0`: stderr below, EXIT:1 (clap value error):

      error: invalid value '0' for '--number <n>': Bad number of commands to undo

      For more information, try '--help'.

- `$S undo -n -1`: stderr below, EXIT:1:

      error: unexpected argument '-1' found

      Usage: stg undo [OPTIONS]

      For more information, try '--help'.

- Stack not initialized: `error: StGit stack not initialized for branch `master``, EXIT:2.
- Detached HEAD: `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached`, EXIT:2.
- After `stg log --clear`: `error: not enough undo information available`, EXIT:2.
- `$S undo -b b2`: clap error `error: unexpected argument '-b' found` + usage, EXIT:1.

## 2. `stg redo`

Help: "If the last command was an undo, the patch stack state will be reset to its
state before the undo." Same options as undo (`-n`, `--hard`, `--color`).

- Output identical in form to undo: single `> <name>` line or nothing; adds log
  entry `redo <n>`.

      $ $S redo            # redid `new: p1`
      > p1
      EXIT:0
      $ $S redo -n 2
      > p3
      EXIT:0

- Redo when nothing to redo (either never undid, or a new stack-modifying command
  such as `pop` was run after the undo): stderr `error: no more redo information available`, EXIT:2.
- Detached HEAD / uninitialized: same errors as undo.

## 3. `stg reset`

Usage (from help, verbatim):

    stg reset [--hard] [<committish> [<patchname>...]]
    stg reset --hard

### Forms
- `$S reset --hard` (no committish): resets index+worktree to the stack head.
  SILENT (no output), EXIT:0, and creates NO log entry. Removes staged-new files
  entirely (a staged `git add`ed new file was deleted from the worktree).
  Works even with detached HEAD (EXIT:0) — the only one of these commands that does.
- `$S reset` (no args at all): clap error, EXIT:1:

      error: the following required arguments were not provided:
        <committish>

      Usage: stg reset [--hard] [<committish> [<patchname>...]]
             stg reset --hard

      For more information, try '--help'.

- `$S reset <state>`: full reset. `<state>` is a committish from `stg log` (short id
  as printed, or full sha, or the full log-commit id). Resets stack metadata, branch
  ref AND worktree to the recorded state (branch commits are rewritten to the
  recorded oids/content; files added later disappear from the worktree).
  Output: just the topmost line, e.g. `> p1`, or nothing if the target state has no
  applied patches. Adds log entry `reset`. EXIT:0.

      $ $S reset d675e47          # state of `new: p1`
      > p1
      EXIT:0
      # reset to `initialize` state: empty stdout, empty stack, branch == initial commit

  Resetting to the CURRENT state still prints `> <top>` and EXIT:0.
  `--hard` may be combined with a committish: `$S reset --hard <state>` works, same output.

- `$S reset <state> <patch>...`: PARTIAL reset — only the named patches are reset to
  their state in `<state>`; everything else keeps its current state. Implemented as a
  real pop/update/push transaction, so the output is full transaction notation:

      $ $S reset d09982c p2       # p2 had been refreshed since state d09982c
      - p2..p3
      & p2
      + p2
      > p3
      EXIT:0
      # p2 commit content reverted; p3 rewritten onto new p2 (new oid); log entry `reset`

  Named patches must exist in the TARGET state, else:
  `error: patch `p2` does not exist`, EXIT:2 (nothing changed).

### Error cases
- `$S reset deadbeef`: `error: invalid committish `deadbeef``, EXIT:2.
- `$S reset HEAD` (a committish that isn't a stack log commit): `error: stack metadata not found`, EXIT:2.
- `$S reset p1` (patch name in committish position): `error: invalid committish `p1``, EXIT:2.
- `$S reset <state> nosuch`: `error: patch `nosuch` does not exist`, EXIT:2.
- With outstanding merge conflicts in the stack: stdout shows partial transaction
  (`- p2..refresh-temp`, `+ p2`, `> refresh-temp`), then stderr
  `error: resolve outstanding conflicts first`, EXIT:2 (state unchanged).
- Detached HEAD with a committish: `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached`, EXIT:2.
- NOT validated against branch: `stg reset <oid-of-another-branch's-log-state>`
  SUCCEEDS and adopts that state on the current branch (master's stack became the
  other branch's stack: patch `pb`, branch head rewritten to `pb`'s commit).

## 4. `stg log`

Options: `-b/--branch`, `-d/--diff`, `-n/--number <n>`, `-f/--full`, `-g/--graphical`,
`--clear`, `--color`; positional `[patch]...`.

### Default format (stdout)
One line per simplified log entry, newest first:

    <short-oid-7>   <RFC2822-date>   <message>

exactly THREE spaces between fields; date like `Fri, 7 Aug 2026 12:11:18 +0000`:

    a3c7bc4   Fri, 7 Aug 2026 12:11:18 +0000   pop
    427facc   Fri, 7 Aug 2026 12:11:18 +0000   refresh p2
    15a9112   Fri, 7 Aug 2026 12:11:18 +0000   refresh refresh-temp (create temporary patch)
    f21bdad   Fri, 7 Aug 2026 12:11:18 +0000   new: p2
    ...
    7b6d282   Fri, 7 Aug 2026 12:11:18 +0000   initialize

Colored (`--color always`, observed via od):
`\e[33m<oid>\e[m   \e[34m<date>   \e[m<msg>\n` — note the reset `\e[m` comes AFTER the
3 spaces following the date. (No leading `\e[0m` here, unlike transaction output.)

### `-n/--number`
- `$S log -n 2` prints the 2 newest entries. `$S log -n 0`: empty output, EXIT:0.
- `$S log -n -1`: EXIT:1, stderr:

      error: unexpected argument '-1' found

        tip: to pass '-1' as a value, use '-- -1'

      Usage: stg log [OPTIONS] [--] [patch]...
             stg log --clear

      For more information, try '--help'.

### `-f/--full`
git-log-style, full oid, `Author:`, git-default date, indented message; entries
separated by one blank line; NO trailing blank line after the last entry:

    commit a3c7bc4334c252741c097f1198b7dce794a9ba38
    Author: Test <t@t.com>
    Date:   Fri Aug 7 12:11:18 2026 +0000

        pop

    commit 427facc75558c2e7496da4bcc9bd7feaf61fd6fe
    ...

### `-d/--diff`
Same header format as `-f`, followed by a git diff of the stack-metadata tree
(`stack.json` and `patches/<name>` files) against the previous simplified entry.
`-d` implies the full format; `-d -f` together == `-d`. Example diff content shows
the patch metadata blob format:

    Bottom: <oid>
    Top:    <oid>
    Author: Test <t@t.com>
    Date:   2026-08-07 12:11:18 +0000

    <commit message>

(blob has NO trailing newline -> `\ No newline at end of file` in diffs;
`stack.json` also has no trailing newline.)

### Patch filtering
- `$S log p1`: only entries where p1's own state/metadata changed
  (e.g. `refresh p1`, `new: p1`; NOT `pop` of another patch, NOT the refresh-temp
  helper entries). `$S log p2 p1`: union, reverse-chronological. `--` separator works.
- Nonexistent patch: `error: patch `nosuch` does not exist`, EXIT:2.

### `--clear`
- `$S log --clear`: SILENT, EXIT:0. Replaces the whole history with a single new
  entry whose message is `clear log` and whose stack.json has `"prev": null`.
  Afterwards `stg undo` fails (`not enough undo information available`) until new
  commands are logged. Works with `-b` for another branch.
- `$S log --clear p1`: EXIT:1, stderr:

      error: the argument '--clear' cannot be used with '[patch]...'
      (+ usage + "For more information, try '--help'.")

### Other
- `$S log -b other` (branch without stack): `error: StGit stack not initialized for branch `other``, EXIT:2.
- `$S log -b nosuch`: `error: branch `nosuch` not found`, EXIT:2.
- Uninitialized current branch: `error: StGit stack not initialized for branch `master``, EXIT:2.
- Detached HEAD: `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached`, EXIT:2.
- `$S log -g` (gitk not installed): `error: could not execute `gitk`: No such file or directory (os error 2)`, EXIT:2.
- Works fine from a subdirectory.

## 5. `stg repair`

Options: only `--color`. No `-b`.

### Consistent stack
Prints the topmost line and still adds a `repair` log entry:

    $ $S repair
    > p1
    EXIT:0
    # log gains: "repair"

If no patches are applied, stdout is empty (EXIT:0).

### Plain `git commit`(s) on top
Converts them to new patches. Name = slugified commit subject: lowercased,
non-alphanumerics -> `-`, collapsed/trimmed dashes
(`"third patch body"` -> `third-patch-body`; `"UPPER CASE Message"` ->
`upper-case-message`; `"fix: something!  weird--name"` -> `fix-something-weird-name`).
Collision with existing patch name gets `-1` suffix (`third-patch-body-1`).

    $ git commit -m "third patch body" ...   # on top of applied patches
    $ $S repair
    > third-patch-body (new)        # stdout
    EXIT:0
    # stderr: info: Creating 1 new patch        (plural: "Creating 2 new patches")
    # log gains TWO entries: "external modifications" then "repair"

New patches become applied at their commit positions (a commit made while p2 was
unapplied yields applied: p1, upper-case-message; unapplied: p2).

### `git reset` making patches unreachable/reachable
- Applied patches no longer reachable: stderr one line per patch, then stdout topmost:

      info: `third-patch-body-1` is now unapplied
      info: `fix-something-weird-name` is now unapplied
      (stdout) > third-patch-body

- Unapplied patches that became reachable: `info: `name` is now applied` lines.

### `git commit --amend` of a patch
The amended commit is unknown, so: `info: `p1` is now unapplied` + `info: Creating 1
new patch`; the amended commit becomes a NEW patch named from its subject (`one`),
old p1 becomes unapplied.

### Merge commit on top
    (stderr)
    warning: 5 patches are hidden below the merge commit 07ad12b7673264a68e59b7b0132689ef78bba52e and will be considered unapplied
    info: `p1` is now unapplied
    ... (one per patch)
    (stdout empty — nothing applied)
    EXIT:0
All patches below the merge become UNAPPLIED (series shows `- name`; despite the word
"hidden" they go to the `unapplied` list).

### Other
- Dirty worktree, consistent stack: succeeds, prints topmost, dirt preserved.
- Detached HEAD: `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached`, EXIT:2.
- Uninitialized: `error: StGit stack not initialized for branch `master``, EXIT:2.

## 6. Cross-cutting notes

- Exit codes: 0 success; 2 = stg runtime errors (`error:`/`warning:`/`info:` on
  stderr); 1 = clap CLI parse errors (usage text on stderr).
- `info:`/`warning:` always go to stderr; transaction output and errors' stdout parts
  as noted. Error prefix coloring with `--color always`:
  `\e[0m\e[1m\e[31merror: \e[0m`\e[0m\e[33m<quoted-command>\e[0m`: ...`
- Transaction marker colors (from undo/pop): `> ` = `\e[34m` (blue), name `\e[1m`
  (bold); `- ` = `\e[35m` (magenta), name `\e[2m` (dim); rolled-back `@ ` = `\e[34m`,
  name bold; each line wrapped in leading `\e[0m` and trailing reset (undo output ends
  with an extra `\e[0m` after the final newline). NO_COLOR did NOT override an
  explicit `--color always`.
- undo/redo/reset-full print ONLY the resulting topmost line; reset-partial and
  failed transactions print full push/pop notation (`+`, `-`, `>`, `&`, `#`, `@`,
  ranges like `- p4..p5`, suffixes like `(new)`, `(conflict)`, `(rolled back)`).
- All five commands work from subdirectories. Only `log` has `-b`; undo/redo/reset/repair
  always operate on the current branch (and all but bare `reset --hard` refuse a
  detached HEAD).

Spec written to `/workspace/observed/undo-redo-reset-log-repair.md` (366 lines, with verbatim outputs/exit codes). Key findings:

**Output model**
- `undo`/`redo`/full-`reset` print exactly one line on success: `> <topmost>` of the resulting state, or *nothing* if no patches are applied. They never print per-patch `+`/`-` lines.
- Partial `reset <state> <patches>...` is a real transaction: prints `- p2..p3`, `& p2`, `+ p2`, `> p3`.
- `repair` prints `> <name> (new)` for new patches; all `info:`/`warning:` go to stderr.

**Surprising behaviors**
- `stg undo` steps back one *log entry*, not one user command: after `stg refresh` (which logs 2 entries: `refresh refresh-temp (create temporary patch)` + `refresh <name>`), a single undo lands in an intermediate state with `refresh-temp` applied on top.
- `stg reset` requires either `--hard` or a committish — bare `stg reset` is a clap error (exit 1) despite the help text implying otherwise.
- `reset <state>` happily accepts another branch's log state and adopts it wholesale on the current branch (no validation).
- Only `reset --hard` (no committish) works on detached HEAD; undo/redo/log/repair all fail with `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached` (exit 2).
- `NO_COLOR` does not override explicit `--color always`.

**Errors**: exit 2 for runtime (`error: not enough undo information available`, `error: no more redo information available`, `error: invalid committish `x``, `error: stack metadata not found`, `error: patch `x` does not exist`); exit 1 for clap parse errors.

**Log**: default line = `<7-char-oid>␣␣␣<RFC2822 date>␣␣␣<msg>`; `-f` = git-log format; `-d` = `-f` + diff of stack-metadata tree (reveals `patches/<name>` blob format: `Bottom:`/`Top:`/`Author:`/`Date:` headers, no trailing newline). `--clear` is silent, leaves a single `clear log` entry with `prev: null`. Log entry messages catalogued (`undo N`, `redo N`, `reset`, `repair`, `external modifications`, `refresh  (CONFLICT)` with double space, etc.).

**Repair**: slugifies commit subjects to patch names (lowercase, dashes, `-1` suffix on collision); logs `external modifications` + `repair` entries; merge commits cause all patches below to become unapplied with a `warning:` line.

**Internals**: `refs/stacks/<branch>` full commit has 3 parents `[simplified-entry, branch-head, prev-full]`; `stg log` prints the simplified (1-parent) commit ids; both forms work as `reset` targets.
